title: Finding (uphams_homehealthcare)
body:
CLAIM: Services that family or unskilled caregivers can perform safely are not covered; family gave medications.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "she lived with her family, who provided support and administered her medications."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.1): "they could safely and effectively be performed by the patient or unskilled caregivers, such services will not be covered"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (12-1251)
body:
CLAIM: Chest pain is a listed sign of cardiac distress that meets the emergency-transport condition.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The ambulance report states that the beneficiary was being transported due to chest pain."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §20): "Exhibits signs and symptoms of acute respiratory distress or cardiac distress such as shortness of breath or chest pain"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (case_excellenthomecare)
body:
CLAIM: Skilled observation must be documented until the condition stabilizes; the beneficiary was stable at discharge.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "based on the general stability of his blood sugar, blood pressure and overall control of his conditions."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.1): "The patient’s necessity for skilled observation must be documented at each home health visit"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (gold_cross_ambulance)
body:
CLAIM: Oxygen is a listed basis, but the record gives no reason it was required.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "However, neither this PCS nor any other document in the record indicates why the oxygen was required."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §20): "Required oxygen or other emergency treatment during transport to the nearest appropriate facility"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (sacredheart_hospital)
body:
CLAIM: The retrieved passages address services related to non-covered services, not inpatient medical necessity, so they do not settle whether the stay was covered.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant billed Medicare for the beneficiary’s inpatient hospitalization from July 27, through July 29, 2005."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §120): "Services "not related to" non-covered services are covered under Medicare."

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (m-11-2450)
body:
CLAIM: Ambulance service to a physician-directed clinic is not covered, and the destination was a clinic staffed by a physician.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The facility to which the appellant was taken on November 2, 2010, is staffed by a physician"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §20): "or a physician-directed clinic is not covered."

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (rx_homecare)
body:
CLAIM: Supervisory visits are administrative, not skilled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "a skilled nurse visited the beneficiary approximately once every two weeks to fill a mediplanner with pills and oversee home health aides."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §70.2): "is an administrative function, not a skilled visit"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (visitingnursing)
body:
CLAIM: Gait training is reasonable and necessary when it can be expected to materially improve or maintain walking ability.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Upon discharge, this score had improved to 18/28, signifying a moderate fall risk."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "are considered reasonable and necessary if they can be expected to materially improve or maintain the patient's ability to walk"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (altabates)
body:
CLAIM: Intensity of 3 hours/day is only asserted by the medical director; recorded therapy minutes are ranges that do not settle it.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He also asserted that the patient received three hours daily of therapy services"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110.2.2): "the provision of intensive therapies at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (midwest_lifeteam)
body:
CLAIM: Transfer was medically appropriate because the transferring hospital lacked needed cardiac services.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The transfer occurred so that the beneficiary would be treated in a hospital where specialist cardiologist services were available."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.4): "the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (rx_homecare)
body:
CLAIM: Skilled nursing visits are not necessary where the nurse only supervises unskilled care and no condition needs observation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the nursing notes do not reveal any significant changes in the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.2): "skilled nursing care would not be considered reasonable and necessary to treat the illness or injury"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (12-1251)
body:
CLAIM: Emergency treatment during transport also establishes necessity.

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

body:

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (state_of_vt)
body:
CLAIM: Wound care by a nurse is skilled nursing when a licensed nurse's skills are needed; a stage II pressure ulcer was treated.

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (eagle_air_med)
body:
CLAIM: Stable condition does not show ground transport was inappropriate.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s vital signs were stable at the time of transfer and she did not experience further significant bleeding while at the originating facility."

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (eagle_air_med)
body:
CLAIM: Distance or obstacles must relate to the nearest appropriate hospital; a closer equipped facility existed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "there was a closer facility equipped to treat the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.1): "Great distances or other obstacles are involved in getting the patient to the nearest hospital with appropriate facilities"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (altabates)
body:
CLAIM: Admission orders are mentioned but preadmission screening and plan of care documentation are not shown.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "However, her physician orders on IRF admission included 13 medications"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (estate_gbr)
body:
CLAIM: Hospital-to-hospital transport requires that the sending hospital lack adequate facilities; the record does not show what service was missing.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The documentation did not state what specific service was not available at the first hospital."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.4): "the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (midwest_lifeteam)
body:
CLAIM: Payment is limited to the distance to the nearer appropriate hospital.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was not taken to the nearest medically-appropriate facility, which would have been a distance of only 133 miles from the transferring facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.6): "the air transport payment is limited to the rate for the distance from the point of pickup to that nearer hospital"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

body:

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (estate_gbr)
body:
CLAIM: Hospital-to-hospital transport is covered only if the destination is the nearest with appropriate facilities.

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.4): "covered only if the hospital to which the patient is transferred is the nearest one with appropriate facilities"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (eagle_air_med)
body:
CLAIM: Where ground transport would have sufficed, payment is based on the ground ambulance amount.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the appellant concedes that “ground transportation to a closer hospital was reasonable” in this case."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §10.4.6): "payment for the air ambulance transport is based on the amount payable for ground ambulance transport"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (altabates)
body:
CLAIM: Therapy intensity approaches or meets the generally accepted standard.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Physical therapy totaling 60-90 minutes per day was provided every weekday."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110.2.2): "intensive therapies at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (prestige_homecare)
body:
CLAIM: Skilled observation is not necessary where fluctuating signs are a longstanding pattern; no medication or plan changes occurred and no skilled teaching was documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the QIC noted that there had been no changes in the beneficiary’s medications or plan of care; in addition, no skilled teaching was documented."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.1): "observation and assessment by a nurse is not reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the illness or injury where fluctuating signs and symptoms"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (gold_cross_ambulance)
body:
CLAIM: Oxygen during transport is a listed condition, but the record does not say why oxygen was required.

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §20): "Required oxygen or other emergency treatment during transport to the nearest appropriate facility"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (midwest_lifeteam)
body:
CLAIM: Cardiac symptoms support emergency presumption.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "where she was diagnosed with cardiac arrhythmia, chest pain and shortness of breath."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.10 §20): "Exhibits signs and symptoms of acute respiratory distress or cardiac distress such as shortness of breath or chest pain"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (state_of_vt)
body:
CLAIM: Wound care by a licensed nurse is skilled, and the record documents observation, cleansing, dressing and caregiver instruction.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the provider’s nurses observed and assessed the pressure ulcer on the beneficiary’s sacrum; provided wound care, including cleansing and dressing the wound"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.8): "Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas, tube sites, and tumor erosion sites)"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (sacredheart_hospital)
body:
CLAIM: Minor, short procedures are outpatient; this was a complicated surgery with a stated need for hospitalization.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was hospitalized “owing to the amount of dissection required intra- abdominally as well as her underlying pulmonary status.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "expected to keep them in the hospital for only a few hours (less than 24)"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (m_12_809)
body:
CLAIM: The beneficiary was formally admitted to inpatient status after initial observation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He was initially placed in observation status but subsequently admitted to inpatient status."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "An inpatient is a person who has been admitted to a hospital for bed occupancy for purposes of receiving inpatient hospital services"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (m-11-1559)
body:
CLAIM: The admission order is the evidence of the decision to admit as inpatient; here the status was reverted to observation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Decision to change from observation to inpt status was made in ERROR."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "The admission order is evidence of the decision by the ordering practitioner to admit the beneficiary to inpatient status"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (kaweah_rehabilitationhospital)
body:
CLAIM: IRF benefit is for patients with complex nursing, medical, and rehabilitation needs, which she had.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She also entered with a stage II pressure sore on her coccyx, with leukocytosis, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "due to the complexity of their nursing, medical management, and rehabilitation needs"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (m_12_809)
body:
CLAIM: Medical predictability of something adverse supports admission.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "During these procedures, the appellant experienced a temporary drop in blood pressure and bradycardia."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "The medical predictability of something adverse happening to the patient"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (m_12_809)
body:
CLAIM: The passages address inpatient admission orders only; they do not settle whether inpatient care was medically necessary. The record shows an observation-to-inpatient transition.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He was initially placed in observation status but subsequently admitted to inpatient status."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "The admission order is evidence of the decision by the ordering practitioner to admit the beneficiary to inpatient status."

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

body:
CLAIM: A condition like diabetes that can adversely affect healing supports the need for skilled wound care.

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

title: Finding (rx_homecare)

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

questions.label: Is the claim supported by that case fact and that policy quote?

body:
CLAIM: Ambulance transport must itself be medically reasonable and necessary; she was treated and released for medication-related nausea.
